conversation: Prepare StepKit for making the repo public and publishing the ready packages to npm. Decisions from the user: publish @stepkit/core, @stepkit/authoring, @stepkit/cli, and @stepkit/create-flows. Do not publish @stepkit/testkit or @stepkit/dashboard yet because they do not have enough useful public surface. Publish @stepkit/create-flows as a sample/general-purpose workflow package, not as personal/local workflows; it should be positioned as use-case-agnostic powerful workflows people can use anywhere. Start publishable packages at version 0.1.0 rather than 1.0.0. Update docs for public release. The README/package READMEs should be useful from node_modules, but not assume agents automatically know where to look. Add a how-to-use/authoring-best-practices skill so agents can understand StepKit usage and authoring conventions. StepKit init should ask whether to auto-install that skill; avoid npm postinstall prompts. The skill should include authoring best practices such as using the continuation model defineWorkflow({ start }), step(...), done(...), workflow-level agents and step-level agent, JSON object inputs, stepkit continue for interactive steps, avoiding manual mutation of .stepkit/runs, using retry instead of invented workflow resume, and using refs correctly. The .stepkit, .claude, agent/skills, skills-lock, and other local agent artifacts should be gitignored/local and untracked unless intentionally included as examples. Remove the repository verification scripts if they are only brittle invariant checks, and clean references to them from docs/CI/AGENTS as needed. Update package metadata and changesets/release posture accordingly. Generate or update public docs/READMEs, add the how-to-use skill, add stepkit init prompt/flags such as --install-skill and --no-install-skill, add tests for CLI behavior and skill content, and run focused/full validations plus npm pack dry-runs for publishable packages. Preserve create-flows source as publishable sample workflows, but remove private/personal language and add needed npm metadata/files/LICENSE/manifest details.
